chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Abu Jameela, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man seek permission to enter upon his father?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes. I used to seek permission to enter upon my father, and my mother was not with him; rather, she was the wife of my father. My mother had died and I was a boy, and there might be matters of their privacy that I did not like to surprise them in, nor would they like that from me. Greeting (with Salam) is more correct and better.'
ai.seo_question: Does a son need to ask permission to enter his father's room if the mother is not there?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the etiquette of *istidhan* (seeking permission) as a general principle of modesty (*haya*) and privacy, extending it to the son-father relationship even in the absence of the mother. He provides a personal precedent, noting that he would seek permission to enter his father's chamber to avoid surprising him during private moments (*khilwa*), thereby emphasizing that the act is rooted in mutual respect rather than mere formality. The Imam concludes by recommending that a verbal greeting of 'Salam' is the most authentic and superior method of entry, balancing social courtesy with the preservation of dignity.
